name: A Bread and Butter Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: currants, picked, washed and dried
ingredients.originalText: a pound of currants, picked, washed and dried

ingredients.name: wine glass of rose water
ingredients.originalText: a wine glass of rose water

instructions.text: Cut some slices of bread and butter moderately thick, omitting the crust; stale bread is best.
Butter a deep dish, and cover the bottom with slices of the buttered bread.
Spread one third of the currants thickly over the bread and butter, and strew on some brown sugar.
Put another layer of bread and butter, and cover it also with currants and sugar.
Finish with a third layer of each.
Beat four eggs very light and mix them with a pint of milk, and a wine glass of rose water.
Pour the mixture over the whole.
Bake the pudding an hour, and grate nutmeg over it when done.
Eat it warm, but not hot.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut some slices of bread and butter moderately thick, omitting the crust; stale bread is best.
2. Butter a deep dish, and cover the bottom with slices of the buttered bread.
3. Spread one third of the currants thickly over the bread and butter, and strew on some brown sugar.
4. Put another layer of bread and butter, and cover it also with currants and sugar.
5. Finish with a third layer of each.
6. Beat four eggs very light and mix them with a pint of milk, and a wine glass of rose water.
7. Pour the mixture over the whole.
8. Bake the pudding an hour, and grate nutmeg over it when done.
9. Eat it warm, but not hot.
